s: Under which Sections of the Press Council Act, 1978 did the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting nominate 13 journalists to the 15th Press Council of India in October 2026?
x: On 17 October 2026 the MIB nominated 13 journalists (six editors and seven working journalists) under Sections 5 and 6 of the Press Council Act, 1978.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council of India:
1. It was first set up in 1966 under the 1965 Act.
2. Its Chairperson is chosen by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, the Lok Sabha Speaker and one member of the Council.
3. It can impose criminal penalties on newspapers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the PCI can only warn, admonish or censure and has no power to impose criminal penalties.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 15th Press Council of India?
o: It has a Chairperson and 28 members.
Its members include 5 MPs: 3 from Lok Sabha and 2 from Rajya Sabha.
Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is its Chairperson since 24 April 2026.
National Press Day is observed on 26 November.
x: National Press Day is observed on 16 November, not 26 November; the other statements are correct.

s: How many members does each Department-Related Standing Committee (DRSC) of Parliament reconstituted for 2026-27 have?
x: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.

s: With reference to the Department-Related Standing Committees reconstituted for 2026-27, which of the following pairs (Chairperson – Committee) is correctly matched?
x: Radha Mohan Singh heads the Defence committee; Bhartruhari Mahtab heads Finance and Shashi Tharoor heads External Affairs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 24 Department-Related Standing Committees reconstituted in October 2026:
1. 16 of them work under the Lok Sabha Speaker and 8 under the Rajya Sabha Chairman.
2. Ministers can be members of these committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: ministers cannot be members of the DRSCs.

s: Who has been appointed Chief Commissioner of the Telangana Senior Citizens Commission in October 2026?
x: Justice E. Tirumala Devi, a retired High Court judge, is the Chief Commissioner for three years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana Senior Citizens Commission:
1. It consists of 1 Chief Commissioner and 2 Commissioners.
2. Government employees neglecting their parents face a 10% salary deduction credited to the parents.
3. It is linked to Article 41 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the salary deduction is 15%, not 10%.

s: Who set up the seven-member committee to revive the Hockey India League in October 2026?
x: The committee to revive the Hockey India League was set up by Mansukh Mandaviya.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hockey India League and related bodies?
o: The Hockey India League began in 2013.
It was revived in 2024 after seven years.
Hockey India was set up in 2013.
FIH was founded in 1924 and is headquartered in Lausanne.
x: Hockey India was set up in 2009, not 2013; the other statements are correct.

s: Who heads the committee formed by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in October 2026 to curb unethical marketing in the pharma sector?
x: The committee is headed by M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog; Preeti Sudan and Naresh Trehan are members.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Pharmaceuticals was established in 2008 under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
2. The NPPA, set up in 1997, fixes drug prices under DPCO-2013.
3. The committee on unethical pharma marketing must report within six months of its first meeting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the report is due within two months of the first meeting.

s: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) regulates drug prices under which order?
x: The NPPA, established in 1997 with headquarters in New Delhi, regulates prices under DPCO-2013.

s: According to the NITI Aayog report of October 2026, India's elderly population is expected to reach how many by 2050?
x: The report projects 347 million elderly by 2050 (about 20.8% of the population), up from 149 million in 2022.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog report on the elderly released in October 2026:
1. The elderly will form about 20.8% of the population by 2050.
2. The elderly population will reach 194 million by 2041.
3. It calls for 1.5 lakh multi-skilled caregivers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the elderly population is projected at 194 million by 2031, not 2041.

s: On which date is the International Day of Older Persons observed?
x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.

s: Who is the Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat set up on 30 October 2026?
x: Suresh N. Patel, former CVC, is the Chairman; Shirish Chandra Murmu and N. S. Vishwanathan are members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat:
1. It was set up on 30 October 2026 and has to give a roadmap in six months.
2. Its Member Secretary is the Joint Secretary (Banking), Department of Financial Services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both statements are correct: the committee was set up on 30 October 2026 with a six-month roadmap deadline and the JS (Banking), DFS as Member Secretary.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Reserve Bank of India and related schemes?
o: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935.
The RBI is headquartered in Mumbai.
The Lead Bank Scheme was launched in 1975.
Sanjay Malhotra is the RBI Governor.
x: The Lead Bank Scheme dates from 1969, not 1975; the other statements are correct.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India
2. Launch of the Lead Bank Scheme
3. Establishment of the NPPA
4. Establishment of the Department of Pharmaceuticals
x: RBI (1935), Lead Bank Scheme (1969), NPPA (1997) and Department of Pharmaceuticals (2008).
